utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is tab 20, sir. Could you please tell me about paragraph 4 and paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 4.1 tells us as follows: According to verified information, a member of the Kosovo Diplomatic Observer Mission, Nick Turnbull, and an unidentified member of the observer team on the 21st and 22nd October this year established contact for the purpose of persuading them to accept the provisions of the agreement on resolving the Kosovo problem, previously signed by representatives of the federal republic of Yugoslavia and the special envoy. The OVK for the time being is refusing to accept the provisions of this agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 5, please. The last portion of paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The very end of this paragraph tells us that the political representative of the OVK abroad Balema Kute [phoen] believes that the Kosovo Liberation Army did not take up its rifles in order to stay under Serbia, this being the message impressed upon the Albanian population. This hard-line wing says, Regardless of any difficulties - meaning difficulties the KLA are facing - we shall never surrender; this is a sacred war; it's now or never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, may this be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00738.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. D008-0801.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a telegram by the security sector of the Pristina Corps, the date is the 5th of November, 1998. 2.6, please. That's page 2 in both versions of the text.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 2.6 talks about the meeting at Sion in Switzerland. There was a meeting of KLA members in supporters in connection with the current situation in Kosovo and Metohija following of the signing of the Milosevic-Holbrooke Agreement. It indicates that the agreed joint NATO KLA tactic is being fully implemented with regard to the withdrawal of our forces, after which they take the territory, link up their forces, and again take control of the territory. It was also said at the meeting that the terrorist activity on the ground should further be stepped-up and new terrorist groups set up and that the enlisting of volunteers should continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this please be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00739.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-810. D008-0810.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a telegram by the security sector of the Pristina Corps dated the 8th November, 1998. 2.1, please. If you can. Just hold on a second until we see the English on our screens. 2.1.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This paragraph of the telegram indicates that there were efforts being made by the international community to deal with the Kosovo crisis in a peaceful way. Along these lines, it tells us that on the 6th of November, 1998, the US ambassador to Macedonia Christopher Hill together with the chief of KDOM Shaun Byrnes established contact with representatives of the Kosovo Liberation Army who were then shown a US plan for a peaceful solution of the Kosovo issue. In terms of time-line, this is perhaps the earliest situation showing that important international players were establishing contact with this terrorist organisation, the KLA, trying to promote or upgrade this terrorist organisation as a party to the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. May this please be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00740.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-0814.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Briefly, please, paragraph 2.1, Defence number 597. Tab 23 for you, sir. Paragraph 2.1, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 2.1 talks about the fact that despite the apparent lull that lasted throughout September following the signing of the agreement, there were again acts of retaliation by the terrorists against both non-Albanian and Albanian people in the area. In the Djakovica area, they are some of the MUP members to go to their villages in order to protect them from terrorists. The same thing was done by people from Decani municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 2.5. This is page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Hold on a second, we'd like to see it in English on our screens too.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Many of the Albanian inhabitants in Kosovo and Metohija, an enormous number of those, in fact, were loyal to the existing authorities. This paragraph shows that they started reporting cases of robbery, property being seised by the terrorists. Their own property. They started reporting this to the MUP. An assessment is presented here which is quite accurate given the escalation of terrorism, that the state did not do everything within its power to protect the Albanian population not involved in any KLA activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00741.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-0820, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a telegram dated the 11th of November, 1998. Security sector at the Pristina Corps again. Sir, could you please do 1.2 for us, comment briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 1.2 describes the fact that members of the so-called Kosovo Liberation Army were taking up positions along the roads gradually controlling the passing traffic, checking travelers, mistreating citizens as well as detaining them, seising vehicles and goods, which led to disquiet on the part of the population. It also says that they were kidnapping some non-Albanians, all of which caused unrest among the non-Albanian population of Kosovo and Metohija. The idea was the first voice for people to try and organise the defence of their own villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this please be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00742.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-0827, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a telegram by the security sector of the Pristina Corps dated the 17th of November, 1998. Sir, briefly, please, 2.2.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, this describes attacks being carried out by the leaders of the KLA against their own fellow Albanians. They were going about villages trying to explain to the people there that it was necessary to immobilise for the war that would come the next spring.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, that's sufficient for our present purposes. May this please be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00743.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-0838. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us wait for the English to come up on our screens first. 2.1, please. That's the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, this talks about the arrogance displayed by the leaders of the KLA, specifically Ramush Haradinaj and his group, visiting Albanian villages, firing barrages and bursts of gun-fire, seising goods, putting across the message that they would kill all those who betrayed them, meaning handing over their weapons to the legal authorities and those working with bodies of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.text: Tab 28 for you, sir. The 15th of December security sector of the Pristina Corps telegram. Sir, just briefly, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It describes a large-scale incident on the border to the Republic of Albania, the Liken border post, specifically. A large number of terrorists were prevented from illegally crossing the state border there. Under the procedures that had been agreed with the OSCE Mission from the moment the agreement was signed on, the Pristina Corps was to report these things to the OSCE. Their mission went to the scene of this incident and photographed the scene, but they refused to sign the Serbian and English records saying that this was not part of the procedure that that their orders were different. General Loncar was the president of the commission for co-operation with the OSCE Mission was informed about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-0875. Tab 29, Defence number 608.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: A telegram by the security sector dated the 15th of December, 1998. 2.1, please, if you can, sir, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, this is the intelligence gathered by the state security service. They arrested terrorists Bajrami, Gazmend. They interrogated him and obtained information indicating that orders by the staff of the KLA, several small terrorists groups, were infiltrated into towns across Kosovo, the idea being to carry out several acts of terror across Kosovo specifically in order to intimidate people and targeting catering establishment including those owned by Albanians who continued to operate. Because these terrorists believed that these Albanians by continued to operate were expressing their support of the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Next page 2.8, please, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This picks up where the previous paragraph left off. It describes the terrorist incident in the town of Pec it itself on the 14th of December, 1998. utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER

utterances.text: General, can you tell us whether illegal arms continued arriving from Albania in late 1998 as well as the training of KLA terrorists in Albania? Did that continue?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC

utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00749.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D008-0900. Tab 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, it's a telegram of the security section of the 24th of December, 1998. 2.1, please comment. Just wait for the English version, please. 2.1 is on the second page at the top.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 2.1, we see information of the 14th Counter-intelligence Group indicating that the leadership of the national movement of Kosovo decided at a meeting held in Switzerland to have the KLA in Kosovo and Metohija put under its control at any cost parts stated here in order to create conditions for the secure supply of weapons from the air by NATO airplanes and helicopters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And tell us what we can see in the last paragraph of 2.1?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At that meeting in relation to that it was stated at the meeting that the Americans instead of a frontal attack suggested the concentration of greater forces at key intersections and roads, as well as in the area specified therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about the last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we see here that there is a connection between this information and the assistance of the KVM, representatives on the full withdrawal of VJ forces and the forces of the MUP from the municipalities of Kacanik, Malisevo, Glogovo, Klina, and Orahovac, which directly correlates with the conclusions of the meeting of the Kosovo national movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00750.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D006-3187.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is a telegram of the 27th of December, 1998, by the security section of the Pristina Corps. Defence number 122. Your tab 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in English page 2, item 2.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That is at the end of page 1 in your copy. Please comment.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We see here information by the SDB concerning a comment by a member of the OSCE Verification Mission, Jean-Pierre Quinton, a Belgian diplomat, that much time will be needed in order to convince individual countries of the correctness of our positions, thus alluding to the USA and Great Britain. The Belgian diplomat considers that there are enough objective reports on the situation in Kosovo and Metohija, having in mind the reports of the Kosovo Verification Mission, but that two of the three people at the top of the mission make a selection among them and send them on according to their country's needs and interests.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00751.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D008-0913. It is Defence number 614. It is a telegram of the Pristina Corps security section dated the 28th of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Comment briefly upon items 2.1.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Item 2.1, it is stated that the latest terrorist acts and killings of Serbs in territory of the municipality of Podujevo caused the remaining Serbs to move out from the few villages inhabited by Serbs in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D00752, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D008-0916. It is Defence document 615.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 36, General. I'd like to hear your comment of item 2.1.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 2.1 of this document, we see information obtained through the application of electronic reconnaissance measures indicating the preparations of terrorists for a spring offensive as well as information about increasing numbers of Albanians moving to Albania and on to some EU countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00753.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D008-0920. Defence number 616.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a telegram of the Pristina Corps security section dated the 9th of January, 1999. Please comment item 3.4. Page 3 in the English as well. 3.4. It begins on this page and then it spills over to page 3. The top.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 3.4, there is mention made of talks under the auspices of members of the OSCE Mission between the terrorists and ourselves in order to have eight military police members released who had been kidnapped during an on-site investigation. There were taken to the terrorist staff in the village of Bare. Richard Ciaglinski participated in on those investigations and upon his return he stated that he was told by the KLA that the KLA will start carrying out attacks against VJ and MUP members in the whole territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00754.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are doing much better. Keep it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I suggest we take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we will now and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. D008-0926. Number 38.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab number 38 for you, sir. It's a telegram by the security sector of the Pristina Corps dated the 13 of January, 1999. Paragraph 2.4, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 2.4 of this document talks about information obtained from several sources to the effect that families of Albanians from Kosovo and Metohija living and working abroad were making suggestions to their relatives in Kosovo and Metohija and warning them in a dramatic fashion to get out of Kosovo and Metohija because soon large-scale terrorist attacks would be launched on the MUP and the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you, yourself, involved in the events described in paragraph 3.3?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the English, please, 3.3. That's the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is the development that I talked about a while ago. Mr. Richard Ciaglinski from the OSCE was there and together we liberated eight members of the military police. This says that on the 13th of January, following several days of negotiations, these men were set free by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this please be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00755.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-0932.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 39, sir. Defence document 618. A telegram by the security sector of the Pristina Corps dated the 19th of January, 1999. Could you please have a look page 2, paragraph 2.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could have that in English as well. Slowly, please, until we see that on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, sir, we don't have that yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2 in the English, please. Paragraph 2.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 2.6 of this document tells us about information suggesting that the OSCE Verification Mission members were making visits to some fringe areas in Kosovo and Metohija, specifically Vitina municipality in this case. They wanted to know about the quality of the bridges in that area and possible landing areas for helicopters. At the time, this caused people to suspect that preparations were referred for the arrival of NATO. There was another source indicating that, as opposed to the previous period of time, the OSCE members were renting flats for 15-day periods which indicated that the OSCE might soon be leaving Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the last page of the English and the Serbian as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, sir, same document last page. 3.2.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see 3.2 in my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. May this be received, please. I was looking at the next document already. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00756.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move on to D008-0943. Tab 40. Defence document 620. A telegram dated the 21st of January, 1992 [as interpreted]. Security sector of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir. Can we focus on 2.2, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 2.2 talks about information having to do with shedding light on the crime of kidnapping of Serbs, Albanians, Roma people, and other nationalities in the area of Prizren. There was an interview with Mazreku, Luan, from Malisevo, he was shown some evidence, photographs, and such, whereupon this person admitted that, along with other members of the KLA from Klina and Orahovac municipality, he had been involved in executing 34 persons from the Prizren area, burning them -- burning them, as the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: 3.2, the last passage, please, if you can. Can we have that in English, please. That's the last page. 3.2.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This portion of the document talks about the fact that there was a meeting in the Prizren barracks, our rank commander, representatives of the OSCE Mission, and we know that each unit had liaison officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please pull down the part where it says the Prizren garrison, like that, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A representative of the OSCE Mr. Mijhalo Krasnosekov admitted to our own liaison officer that he had gone with Walker to the village of Racak and that he had personally counted a total of 26 dead bodies in civilian clothes but with weapons and KLA insignia. He said that we had won that battle in the military sense but that we had lost in a political sense, meaning that NATO would be bombing us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this please be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00757.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-0958. The 20th of February, 1998. Defence document 622, tab 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's a telegram by the 14th Counter-intelligence Group, the 22nd of February, 1999, dispatched to, among others, the security sector of the Pristina Corps. Could you please briefly comment on the first two paragraphs in the briefest possible terms.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a period that coincided with the negotiations at Rambouillet. This shows that the terrorist organisations, specifically the KLA as the political wing over in Switzerland, had no intention of giving up, putting up armed resistance in order to try and achieve their goals. Therefore, volunteers are still being dispatched to Albania's north; the leaders of the KLA found it unacceptable that the Albanian delegation at Rambouillet would accept the disarming of the KLA, and they would not allow Kosovo to remain in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could just briefly comment on the last paragraph on this page.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This confirms that the terrorists were carrying out preparations for an offensive and was going on across all the village Kosovska Mitrovica municipality, those inhabited by Albanians. There was a curfew that was imposed --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry, sir. I'm talking about the previous document, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph on page 1 talks about Azem Vllasi's position; he was one of the leaders of Kosovo Albanians, that the Albanian delegation in Rambouillet could not make sure that autonomy was achieved in keeping with the 1974 constitution, let alone independence in any shape or form. He was, however, convinced that NATO would be arriving in Kosovo and Metohija but as peacekeeping forces, or else their arrival would be preceded by air-strikes against the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document please be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00758.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-0961. Defence document 623, tab 42, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: A telegram received by the security sector of the Pristina Corps and dispatched by the 14th Counter-intelligence Group on the 25th February, 1999. If you can, sir, please, at paragraph 3, in relation to the 23rd February, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed. It talks about terrorists groups from the Drenica area which was the strongest -- the major extremists' stronghold throughout the clashes in Kosovo. They ordered all Albanians in the village of Brusnik to leave the village by the 24th of February, Brusnik was predominantly Albanian, because they planned to conduct combat operations in that area over the following days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this please be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00759.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D008-0964. 65 ter number 624.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: A telegram by the 3rd Army Command security department dated the 1st of March, 1999. Could you please comment on paragraph 1. Just to make sure we have both on our screens -- that's right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The paragraph talks about the fact that late in February 1999 there were Albanians gathering around the Djeneral Jankovic border crossing to the Republic of Macedonia. They asked the border police to allow them to cross into the Republic of Macedonia, saying that there was an imminent outbreak of large-scale hostilities between the terrorists and the VJ along the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: 2.5 of the same document, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This paragraph talks about continuing acts of provocation by the Albanian terrorists targeting the local security members in the village of Osek Hilja. As you know, there were attempts being made to overcome the crisis from July 1998 on, and then a multi-ethnic police force was established in some villages across Kosovo meant to reduce tensions and regain the trust of the local Albanian population by having their representatives in the authorities. But they refused to go along with that. Instead, they attacked some members of this multi-ethnic police force. That's what the paragraph tells us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00760.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D008-0968. Defence document 625.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: For you, sir, tab 44. A telegram by the security sector of the 3rd Army dated the 2nd March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 2.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Page 2 in your document, sir.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 2.6 tells us that there was pressure being exerted by the terrorist forces of KLA on Serb villages of Podujevo in the municipality, forcing people to leave their homes. The intention being to set those homes ablaze once the people left. We are talking here about the village of Pirane and other Serb inhabited villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, 2.6. I'm not sure if we are looking at the same document. I'm talking about the 2nd of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 44, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you please read 2.6, how it begins?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Following an order by the terrorists of the so-called KLA on the 27th of February this year, a large number of residents of the village of Pirane, presently [indiscernible] left their homes, leaving at least some 30 families behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you just comment?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, one can see here that in addition to expelling non-Albanians, the terrorists did not shy away from driving out some Albanians from their own villages in order to achieve their own goals. They also burned down some homes which shows that they were certainly not averse to looting, themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 2.7, please, if you could have a look. That's the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We had several sources suggesting that members of the Verification Mission, primarily those from the US contingent, to a large extent were providing the logistical assistance for the benefit of the terrorists in terms of sharing information with them. And they were in charge of monitoring the overall situation in Kosovo and Metohija. Therefore, that is the information presented here. They were also adamant that the terrorists should reduce their activities before the Rambouillet conference on the 15th of March in order to avoid them being blamed for an escalation -- for a potential escalation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document please be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00761.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have D008-0974. It is Defence document 626.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Your tab 45. Yes, 45. Can you comment on this telegram of the 14th Counter-intelligence Group dated 5 March 1999 sent, amongst others, to your intelligence section.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This telegram is about a meeting held in Macedonia between Robert Dole, an American congressman, and a delegation of Albanian political parties, as well as the KLA terrorist organisation delegation. The meeting was attended by the leaders of Albanian political parties, but what we can note is that Hashim Thaqi was not there on behalf of the KLA. As we see later, he was the only person against the signing of that agreement. Ibrahim Rugova, as well as the Democratic League of Kosovo, as a moderate wing in favour of a peaceful solution to the Kosovo crisis, left open the possibility for the Kosovar delegation in Rambouillet to be able to sign such an agreement but that such an agreement would not be binding on the KLA to accept any disarmament. There's also an assessment provided that Naim Jerliu, one of the political leaders, stated his suspicion for Hashim Thaqi not being present because he knew that there would be some pressure exerted upon him to sign it. It says here, literally, He is an American player and as such will not accept the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00762.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have D006-3247. Document number 181.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 46. This is a telegram of the 2nd Army intelligence section -- sorry, the 3rd Army, dated the 5th of March, 1999. Could you comment item 2.2.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In this item we have information about terrorist preparations in the area of Drenica for an offensive. This is dated the 5th of March, 1999. What is also mentioned is that there would be a general mobilisation of all able-bodied Albanians who were to be armed and dispatched to different KLA units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A brief comment of 2.3 as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Here we have information gathered by the SDB about a multi-member delegation of the Albanian lobby on the 3rd of March, 1999, attended a meeting in the White House where, apart from the US state top political leaders, there were also people present from national security and armed forces. This concerns the talks in Rambouillet. The Albanian delegation received guarantees that, in the political part of the agreement, nothing will be changed. What is key is that the Albanian delegation required guarantees that after the signing of the agreement, there will be no changes concerning the disarmament of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00763.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D008-0981.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a telegram of the 6th of March, 1999, by the security department of the 3rd Army Command. Could you please comment item 2.2.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There is mention made of illegal incursions of foreign mercenaries from Albania into Kosovo and Metohija from Islamic countries. There is information that one such group was in the area of Kacanik. What was characteristic of the situation throughout 1998 and 1999 was that the terrorist staffs collected financial aid from the Albanian population by force as well as required that they be supplied with foodstuffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we next go to 2.1.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to operative data collected all terrorist headquarters in Kosovo and Metohija were ordered to carry out intensive liquidations of Albanian individuals who are members of the local police. I've already referred to the multi-ethnic police force. This is the police force referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00764.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Document D008-0985, tab 48. Defence document 629.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is a telegram by the security section of the 3rd Army Command dated 13 March 1999. Please comment on item 2.2.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This document also points to the aggressive approach of KLA members towards their ethnicity in order to force them to mobilised. This concerns the villages in the surroundings of Prizren. Terrorists entered houses and issued threats due to which certain locals were forced to flee, since some of them wanted to avoid being mobilised or liquidated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about item 2.3? Tell us something about that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Information contained in 2.3 has to do with OSCE Verification Mission members organising transportation of food articles for the KLA as well as their wounded to certain locations, in particular the village of Ljubovac in Srbica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We can see, I believe, that your security section of the Pristina Corps sent daily reports to the security section of the 3rd Army in relation to Kosovo and Metohija and the three items you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What we see in these reports is the information you had forwarded to the security section of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say that exactly, sitting here today, because in addition to receiving information from us, they also received information from the security organs of the military district of Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00765.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D008-0990. It is tab 49, 65 ter number 630.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Item 2.3, please comment.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In item 3.2 [as interpreted] we have information about representatives of the KVM in Suva Reka insisted in getting regional terrorist leaders to use new code-names as well as numerical codes in their internal communications with members of the mission. And in contact with the verifiers about the whereabouts of certain terrorists groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00766.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Petersen.

utterances.speaker: MS. PETERSEN
utterances.text: I'm just noticing with this document, it's from the command of the 3rd Army security department, and I thought the specific paragraph we're talking about was information from the state security service. So I'm just wondering if, in this one, if this witness has personal knowledge of the contents of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You've heard my learned friend. Can you please address that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There was always an exchange of information between us and the 3rd Army security section and back, as well as including the state security service in their exchange of information with my service and the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at item 2.2 on the second page. In the English as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I ran ahead of myself. It's the next document. First I'd like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe it's an exhibit now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I apologise. D008-0994, please. It is Defence number 631.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 50 for you, Witness. This is another telegram of the 3rd Army Command security section dated 22 March 1999. Please look at 1.1.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1.1 there's information by the Nis Corps and their security organ about the village of Lojane which is in Serbia proper -- or, sorry, in the territory of the Republic of Macedonia that there had been a collection centre formed for NATO intelligence analysis where Albanian individuals are being interviewed who had crossed into Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00767.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Document D008-1695.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tab 51. Defence document 642. It's a telegram dated 29 March 1999 by the security section. Sorry, 3rd Army Command. Item 1.1, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a combat report of the 3rd Army Command sent to the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army dated 29 March. There is information about the complex security situation in the country. In item 1.1, it is stated that the border units of the neighbouring countries remain at full combat readiness levels in the general area of Bajram Curi and Tropoja where there is a group of NATO officers conducting training of Siptar terrorist groups as well as creating lists of Siptar volunteers that are dispatched to the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00768.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have Prosecution document 02811 on the 65 ter list. It is a report of the Pristina Corps Command dated the 30th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is tab 52, witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's already an exhibit. P1466.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm interested in item 1.1(b). "During the 29th of March ..." Can you see that part?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. During the 29th of March, a strong terrorist group was inserted from the Republic of Albania into the sector of the Mitar Vojnovic border post. It was detected and broken up, in the course of which 13 terrorists were killed. Part of the terrorists had NATO uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about item 5, security situation? Can you comment upon that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Item 5, security situation. It is stated that in the units within the area of responsibility of the Pristina Corps detected an increase in crime levels caused by an increase in the number of reservists and people from Territorial Defence detachments. There is also information there on criminal reports submitted per personnel category.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document. I am sorry, it's already been admitted.

utterances.text: What is the correct exhibit number for that document? Is it P466?
